lead.headline: India's wholesale inflation hits 12.3% in October, driven by energy
signal: If Brent stays lower, WPI pressure should ease after the festive period, with a lag in CPI.
Manufacturers facing higher input costs are likely to raise prices, which keeps retail inflation sticky.
lead.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
lead.hook: India's wholesale inflation rose to ==12.3% in October==, from 11.4% in September, as fuel and power prices rose 32.84% year on year.
points: WPI (Wholesale Price Index, prices businesses pay each other) rose 12.3% in October versus 11.4% in September.
Fuel and Power inflation was 32.84%, up from 25.85%. Crude petroleum and natural gas inflation reached 70.80%.
Manufactured products eased to 9.54% from 9.76%; food inflation eased to 8.58% from 8.66%. So the surge is narrow: energy.
Bank of Baroda's Madan Sabnavis says firms have passed on only part of input costs, so retail core inflation (CPI) will carry the rest in coming months.
Brickwork's Pranjal Ghate notes Brent crude fell about $20 a barrel by mid-November and expects CPI to peak near 6% in Q3 FY27, above RBI's 4% target; he sees a 25 bp repo hike to 5.75%.
lead.editors_read: This is an energy shock, not broad inflation: food and manufacturing eased. The risk is second-round pass-through, as firms raise prices to recover costs, which keeps RBI tightening even after oil falls. Weak monsoon and higher rates together hit rural demand.
lead.evidence_of: Energy price shock is forcing India to tighten

frontpage.headline: India joins US-led pact to secure AI supply chains
signal: The aim is to reduce dependence on adversary countries for minerals, models and chips as the US competes with China.
frontpage.hook: India and nine other countries signed the ==San Francisco Declaration== to jointly protect AI technologies and infrastructure, the US state department said.
points: Signatories: US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, UAE and UK.
The declaration says economic security underpins national security and calls for joint protection of sensitive technologies and AI infrastructure.
Working groups will cover AI policy, adoption, supply chains, security hubs and resilience.
It builds on Pax Silica, launched last year to secure supply chains for AI models, chips and critical minerals, with joint projects and coordinated export controls.
frontpage.editors_read: India gains access to a US-aligned tech bloc, but export controls are the price of entry: Indian firms may face stricter rules on who they sell chips and AI to. It is also the context for Nvidia's China leakage scandal today.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

frontpage.headline: Firm tied to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered ~$12B in Nvidia chip orders for China
signal: If Culper's estimate holds, Nvidia's China exposure is much larger than reported.
frontpage.hook: Megaspeed arranged nearly ==$12 billion of Nvidia chip orders for Chinese firms== between March 2024 and June 2025, the Wall Street Journal reports.
points: Orders covered several hundred thousand chips that US export controls aimed to keep out of China.
Megaspeed is owned by Alice Huang, former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The company says she left on August 30, 2025.
It reportedly got scarce chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because Alibaba was a major client.
Nvidia reported $12.4 billion China revenue over six months, 7% of total; short-seller Culper estimates over 20% last fiscal year, possibly via indirect channels.
Megaspeed says it conducted lawful business and has hired counsel for an internal investigation.
frontpage.editors_read: Export controls fail at resellers, not at the chipmaker's headline sales. Expect rules to target cloud partners and intermediaries. Separately today, Treasury is demanding answers from Nvidia.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

frontpage.headline: Ukraine's biggest drone attack: Russia says it intercepted 1,336
signal: Mass cheap drones are now a revenue weapon against Russian refining, not only battlefield tools.
frontpage.hook: Russia says it intercepted ==1,336 Ukrainian drones== on Monday, apparently Kyiv's largest aerial assault since the full-scale invasion began nearly five years ago.
points: Recent Ukrainian operations have involved more than 1,000 drones, aimed at Russia, Crimea and the Black and Azov seas.
Strikes increasingly target oil refineries; Zelenskyy claims over 55% of Russian refining capacity is knocked out (unverified, Russia hasn't responded).
Ukraine blames recent speed restrictions on US-made Starshield satellites for weakening its air defence.
Russia keeps hitting Ukraine's power grid. US-mediated talks have produced no breakthrough.
Damage from the latest strikes is unclear; Russia rarely discloses it.
frontpage.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

frontpage.headline: Jio in talks with ISRO, Skyroot for 1,600-satellite constellation
signal: If Indian rockets win, it is a large domestic launch order for Skyroot and ISRO.
frontpage.hook: Jio Platforms is talking to ISRO, Skyroot and other Indian launchers to deploy ==a 1,600-satellite low Earth orbit constellation==, Mint reports.
points: Jio wants domestic launch options first, with SpaceX also considered; it is assessing whether to do design through operations in India.
Plan: test launch of a handful of satellites in September 2027, mass deployment from early 2028, 400-450 satellites by 2030, full constellation by 2035.
An initial batch of about 390 satellites would launch in phases, with 23 ground stations in India.
Rivals: Starlink, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, and Amazon Leo seeking entry. Jio's services still await government clearances.
ISRO's LVM3 launched 72 OneWeb satellites in 2022-23.
frontpage.evidence_of: Telecom giants are building their own satellite networks

frontpage.headline: Trump says US-India trade deal 'very close'
signal: No tariff or product details were given, so treat 'very close' as unconfirmed until text is published.
frontpage.hook: Trump told reporters a trade deal with India is =='very close'== after meeting Modi at the G7 in France, though no terms were given.
points: Trump called ties 'stronger than ever' and said Modi is 'a very tough negotiator'.
He said the US would help if India were attacked.
He backed continued opportunities for skilled Indian professionals in the US.
Modi stressed keeping the Strait of Hormuz open for global trade.

frontpage.headline: India's 2026 monsoon: 87% of normal, 44% of districts deficient
signal: Rain-fed rice, cotton, soybean and pulses in the Deccan face income and groundwater stress, adding to food and rate pressure.
frontpage.hook: The 2026 monsoon ended at ==87% of the long-period average==, the 13th weakest since 1901, with 44% of districts deficient, the most since 2015.
points: Rainfall was 759.4 mm; 30 of 36 subdivisions got less than in 2025.
Marathwada rainfall fell 56% to 389 mm, North Interior Karnataka 54%, Telangana 39%, West Rajasthan and Punjab 58%.
June was worst: 25 of 36 subdivisions fell short during kharif sowing. 77 of 144 subdivision-months were deficient, versus 58 in 2018.
14 low-pressure systems formed, above the ~13 average, yet rain was low, so system counts don't predict rainfall.
Jammu and Kashmir and parts of Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal got more rain.
frontpage.evidence_of: Energy price shock is forcing India to tighten

frontpage.headline: MIT: timed pink noise strengthens brain's sleep cleaning waves
signal: The step to clinical benefit in Alzheimer's is unproven; next studies must show waste clearance.
frontpage.hook: MIT researchers used ==50-millisecond bursts of pink noise== timed to slow brain waves to enlarge cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) waves during sleep in 14 healthy volunteers.
points: During sleep, CSF waves help clear waste such as amyloid beta. They follow slow electrical brain waves.
Sounds delivered at the peak of a slow wave enlarged both the electrical and CSF waves without waking participants.
The team built an EEG method removing fMRI interference in under 100 ms, plus an algorithm predicting the next peak.
The study did not show more waste was cleared or that sleep improved.
Lead author Joshua Levitt has launched a company to develop a home headband.
frontpage.evidence_of: Brain research is finding non-drug levers

stories.headline: SEBI to issue AI guidelines with human oversight for market firms
signal: Brokers and advisers using AI will likely need disclosure, audit and fallback systems; compliance work for vendors.
stories.hook: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said ==detailed AI guidelines== are coming for capital markets, including human-in-the-loop oversight; no timeline was given.
points: SEBI is reviewing its framework so AI use doesn't compromise investor protection or market integrity.
Since December 2024, regulated firms are solely responsible for AI outputs and data privacy, whether built or bought.
A June 2025 consultation proposed client disclosure of AI use, vendor accountability, independent audits, testing, five-year data retention and fairness rules.
It flagged deepfakes, reliance on few AI providers, herding and runaway AI, suggesting kill switches and circuit breakers.
Pandey says human oversight alone isn't enough: 'an AI-generated alert is not a finding'. SEBI's Sudarshan tool has flagged over 20,000 fraudulent posts since November 2025.
stories.evidence_of: Governments move to regulate rogue AI agents

stories.headline: Bessent demands outside CEO and export probe at Nvidia
signal: Expect tighter chip export legislation and compliance costs for chip sellers.
stories.hook: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia needs a =='dramatic shake-up'==, an external CEO, and answers on export compliance within 10 days.
points: Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after revelations of alleged affairs, including one with Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset.
Bessent asked whether Singapore-based intermediaries were allowed to supply chips to China and who at Nvidia knew.
He blamed the Commerce Department for delaying blacklisting Megaspeed; Congressional committees want Huang to testify.
Arm CEO Rene Haas has reportedly been approached; Lisa Su is mentioned; interim CEO is Colette Kress.
stories.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

stories.headline: India gets 12.8% of deep tech rounds but 1.6% of capital
signal: Large buyers like NTPC and Indian Oil can help startups by agreeing pilot success terms and purchase timing upfront.
stories.hook: India's deep tech startups raised $914 million in 2025, ==12.8% of global rounds but only 1.6% of capital==, per Speciale Invest.
points: For every 100 seed rounds in India there were 23 Series A and B rounds, versus 105 globally.
January-August 2026 Series A/B rounds averaged $11.5 million in India versus $55.5 million globally.
Space and life sciences are best placed to scale; semiconductors and batteries depend on imported fabrication, cells and materials.
The ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund could help; the Technology Development Board allocated ₹2,192 crore to 22 projects in round one.
stories.evidence_of: Indian deep tech raises more seeds than growth capital

stories.headline: VanDyke case exposes gaps in India's handling of drone trainers
signal: Expect pressure for drone end-use checks and rules on foreign security trainers near borders.
stories.hook: A Delhi court granted default bail to American Matthew VanDyke and six Ukrainians after the NIA's ==UAPA investigation outran its 180-day window==.
points: NIA alleges they entered Mizoram without permits and crossed into Myanmar to train armed groups in drone warfare.
VanDyke was arrested on 13 March 2026; the chargesheet on 8 September covered only immigration offences, not UAPA.
Default bail was granted on 18 September; on 25 September they could travel home for a month. Bail is not an acquittal.
No evidence has been shown of a link to Indian insurgents or foreign state sponsorship.
stories.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

stories.headline: IBM in talks with two more states for quantum tie-ups
signal: States are competing to host quantum hardware.
stories.hook: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said ==at least two more state partnerships== are in the works like Amaravati's quantum computer, due early next year.
points: Amaravati components arrive this month; installation follows early next year.
IBM has committed $10 billion to quantum globally over five years, part for India; it invests about $3 billion a year in India.
Krishna cited four use areas: materials and chemistry, optimisation, weather and fluid equations, and machine learning.
He made no new financial commitment.

also.line: Pakistan tested its indigenous Fa'az air-to-air missile, a possible shift from Chinese and American suppliers, though imported missiles like PL-15 remain the backbone of its inventory.
also.source: Defence BREAKING NEWS | Defence LATEST NEWS | Defence NEWS TODAY | Defence LIVE UPDATES | Defence TRENDING NEWS | – ThePrint

stories.headline: Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon satellites
signal: A months-long grounding deepens the launch bottleneck, which helps Indian launchers like Skyroot if they can scale.
stories.hook: ULA's Vulcan failed about 10 minutes after launch, ==destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites== in the company's first mission failure.
points: Cause is unknown; the failure appeared after second-stage separation. Blue Origin, which supplies the BE-4 engines, is helping investigate.
It was Vulcan's fifth flight and first in nine months; the Pentagon had not yet cleared it for national security payloads.
Amazon has deployed 398 satellites over 14 launches, about 12% of the 3,236 needed.
SpaceX's Starlink has over 11,000 satellites and owns its rockets; SpaceX is no longer accepting Falcon 9 bookings.
stories.evidence_of: Launch capacity is the satellite bottleneck

also.line: Baidu's third-quarter net profit fell 46% as a search advertising slump outweighed AI growth (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: India faces a more painful return to higher interest rates
signal: Rural demand is most at risk because farm prospects are worse and inflation higher there.
stories.hook: Economists expect RBI to raise rates another ==50 to 75 basis points==, from 5.5% to as high as 6.25%.
points: Oil near $100 a barrel, weak consumers and fragile global sentiment make this cycle harder than 2024-25.
ICRA's Aditi Nayar expects inflation above 6% for the next couple of months, making a December hike 'almost certain'; HSBC expects 50 bp.
GDP grew 7.8% in April-June, giving room to trade demand for price stability.
Foreign investors pulled over $30 billion this year through October; net outflows are about $23 billion. The rupee hit nearly 97 per dollar last month.
The trade deficit hit a one-year high in October.
stories.evidence_of: Energy price shock is forcing India to tighten

stories.headline: RBI seeks review of Supreme Court's Yes Bank AT-1 ruling
signal: If the ruling stands, AT-1 holders gain protection and banks may find these bonds costlier.
stories.hook: RBI has asked the Supreme Court to review its 15 October order that voided the ==₹8,415 crore write-down== of Yes Bank AT-1 bonds.
points: RBI says the court missed errors on Basel III loss-absorption rules and the difference between pre-specified and PONV triggers.
It warns restoring the bonds __could dilute capital infused in 2020 and weaken__ AT-1 loss absorption across banks.
It seeks open-court hearing and a stay; Yes Bank filed its own review on 13 November.
Court held the administrator couldn't write down bonds once the reconstruction scheme took effect without a clause for it.

stories.headline: IIFCL lends Yotta ₹2,948 crore with tough terms as debt tops $1.4B
signal: Lenders are asking for hardware collateral as AI infrastructure debt grows.
stories.hook: State lender IIFCL gave Yotta a ==₹2,948 crore loan== for a Noida data centre, with terms that let it seize Nvidia chips on default.
points: Loan runs 15 years for the 61 MW 'D2' facility, project cost ₹3,879 crore; promoters fund ₹931 crore.
The promoter must eventually own the B300 GPUs; Yotta must show proof of clients to receive the final 20%.
Yotta's net long-term borrowings are ₹13,488 crore. Crisil said debt __could reach up to ₹12,000 crore by March__ 2027 without equity.
India Ratings flags long debt tenures against short GPU lifespans. Yotta says GPUs are financed separately.
Yotta targets raising up to $1.5 billion this fiscal year, including a $400 million IPO by March 2027.
stories.evidence_of: AI data-centre build-out is running on debt

stories.headline: India's unemployment rate eases to 4.9% in October
signal: Gains come from rural women's participation, not urban jobs, which remain at 6.7% unemployment.
stories.hook: India's unemployment rate fell to ==4.9% in October== from 5% in September, and 5.2% a year earlier, PLFS data shows.
points: Urban unemployment fell to 6.7% from 6.9%; rural stayed at 4.2%.
Female labour force participation rose to 35% from 34.6%, its highest since February 2026; rural female participation was 39.5%.
Overall participation was 55.7% and worker population ratio 53%.
Survey covered 3,70,475 people.

stories.headline: India and Egypt agree to explore a trade pact targeting $12B trade
signal: Egypt's location between the Mediterranean and Red Seas gives Indian exporters access to Africa, Arab and European markets.
stories.hook: India and Egypt agreed to explore a preferential or free trade agreement aiming for ==$12 billion in bilateral trade==.
points: Trade rose 35% to $6.5 billion in FY2025-26 and 65% to $5.04 billion in April-September 2026.
A Joint Working Group will draft terms of reference.
Indian investments in Egypt exceed $5.5 billion.
Priority sectors include pharma, fertilisers, engineering, textiles and renewable energy; 300+ companies attended a business forum.

also.line: The Prince and Princess of Wales began a three-day India visit, their first joint overseas trip in four years, with a Modi meeting and Earthshot Prize events planned.

stories.headline: Iran escalates drone attacks as Trump waits
signal: Prolonged Hormuz disruption keeps oil prices elevated, with direct effects on India's inflation.
stories.hook: Bahrain intercepted ==Iranian drones twice in three days== as Iran pushes Gulf states while US blockade squeezes its economy.
points: Iran's IRGC claimed an attack on a US helicopter base in Bahrain; the US embassy urged heightened vigilance.
Iran rejects Gulf compensation demands and warned against reopening 'old wounds'.
Gulf oil exports were 18.4 million barrels a day in October, about 26% below prewar levels (IEA); Iran has exported no meaningful crude for over two months.
Trump said 'we don't need a deal with Iran' and cancelled Vance's effort to revive talks.
Fuel shortages and protests in Bandar Abbas; Iran refuses to discuss enrichment.

stories.headline: Burnham says Brexit 'has not worked', will sign new EU deal
signal: Closer alignment could ease trade frictions for Indian firms exporting to Europe via the UK.
stories.hook: UK PM Andy Burnham says Brexit =='has not worked'== and he'll sign an EU deal that he says could raise GDP by 0.4%, about £17bn.
points: Talks this week cover food and farming, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme.
He will sign if it fits Labour's manifesto and red lines, improves the Brexit deal and delivers tangible gains.
EU relations minister Falconer says the UK would have a voice but no vote on EU food policy, and an exit clause is likely.
Boris Johnson says Britain would vote for Brexit again.

stories.headline: India's WPI inflation hits 12.29% in October on fuel
signal: Input costs for chemicals, metals and plastics suggest further price pass-through.
stories.hook: India's wholesale inflation rose to ==12.29% in October==, above a Reuters poll forecast of 12.1% and 11.39% in September.
points: Fuel and power inflation was 32.84%; mineral oils 45.57%; crude and gas 70.80%.
Electricity inflation turned positive at 8.06% from -0.43%.
Chemicals inflation was 17.53%, basic metals 17.21%.
November data is due December 14.
stories.evidence_of: Energy price shock is forcing India to tighten

also.line: AI cheating fears spook South Korea ahead of its high-stakes college entrance exam (source unreachable — headline only).

stories.headline: Renewable power is outpacing India's grid
signal: Aligning plant commissioning with transmission completion would reduce waits and wasted power.
stories.hook: An IRENA-CREEI report says India's solar and wind plants can be built faster than transmission, leaving ==finished plants waiting to connect== or power curtailed.
points: Better use of existing lines, through dynamic line ratings and flow-control equipment, can help while new lines are built.
Batteries, pumped hydro and flexible demand move power across time; in China, joint operation of a hydropower and solar plant used 99% of solar output.
With more inverter-based power, grids need grid-forming inverters and synchronous condensers for stability.
Availability-based payments to transmission assets can attract private capital.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: PLI adds 24 GW to India's solar module capacity: NITI Aayog
signal: Success depends on domestic sourcing and cost competitiveness against Chinese producers.
stories.hook: India's solar module capacity grew nearly 15-fold to ==about 116 GW==, with PLI-backed projects contributing around 24 GW.
points: PLI projects are 20.7% of capacity; the scheme has ₹24,000 crore allocated and ₹64,873 crore investment by March 2026.
Module imports fell from $4.35B in 2023-24 to $2.15B in 2024-25; exports hit $1.97B in 2023-24, then $1.12B in 2024-25.
Falling global prices, Chinese pricing and China's supply chain dominance are challenges.
Employment and production effects are still developing.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: India's EV sales grow 66.6% in Q2 FY27
signal: Heavy trucks are the fastest-growing category, though from a small base.
stories.hook: India's EV sales grew ==66.6% year on year== in July-September 2026.
points: All categories except e-cart grew quarter on quarter; e-HCV rose 309.25%.
All except e-rickshaw grew year on year; e-HCV grew 739.4%.
Five states, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, made 52.8% of e-2W sales.

also.line: Indian solar makers are finding that moving from module assembly to cells needs far more capital and technology, which may push smaller players into partnerships (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Apple and OpenEvidence launch experimental AI health chat study
signal: Apple is testing conversational health AI before any product commitment.
stories.hook: Apple and OpenEvidence launched a ==study of an experimental AI health chat app== at the HLTH conference.
points: It studies user trust, comprehension and response quality.
Apple's Sumbul Desai says it chose a clinically grounded partner.
OpenEvidence's CEO says it is trusted by doctors and Apple by consumers.

stories.headline: US global health aid is changing, not ending
signal: Aid becomes bilateral and conditional.
stories.hook: Congress kept about ==$10 billion for global health programs==, now run under an 'America First' strategy with strings attached.
points: US withdrew from WHO and paused aid; reporters documented drug shortages and clinic closures.
The September strategy asks recipient countries to take more responsibility.
Countries are invited to negotiate 'America First' agreements; some are balking.

stories.headline: Versant, Lilly back $100M startup for non-viral gene delivery
signal: Non-viral delivery would allow repeat dosing if it works.
stories.hook: Versant, Eli Lilly and others put ==$100 million into Seawolf Therapeutics==, which aims to deliver genes without viruses.
points: Sanofi also signed a partnership with the company.
Viral delivery allows only one dose because patients develop antibodies, and high doses can cause serious side effects.

also.line: John Doerr is backing Tom Health, an AI primary-care company named after his late brother, spun out of Lumeris (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Livestock work is driving women's growth in Indian agriculture
signal: Dairy and livestock programmes now reach women more than crop schemes do.
stories.hook: Nearly ==25% of female farm workers== now work in animal husbandry, versus 5% of male farm workers.
points: Women's farm employment has risen sharply since 2018 to a record.
Over four in ten women work in cereals, pulses and oilseeds, but that share is falling.
Mixed farming has also risen as a share of women's employment.

also.line: Experts demand a ₹1.66 lakh crore drought relief package and full farm loan waiver for 304 affected talukas in Maharashtra (summary from limited source text).
